title: JANUS Engine R2B — direct artificial-gill to PEM fuel-cell gate
purpose: Evaluate the minimum-complexity JANUS self-drive path in which dissolved oxygen passes through an oxygen-permeable artificial-gill membrane into a low-pO2 recirculating gas loop feeding a PEM fuel cell. Bulk O2/N2 separation, sorbent cycling and LOX are bypassed in the first self-drive screen.
architecture: water -> artificial gill -> recirculating low-pO2 gas -> PEMFC cathode -> moisture/heat management -> recirculating gas return
energy_boundary: Hydrogen or another explicit fuel remains the primary stored chemical energy source. Dissolved oxygen is the environmental oxidizer. No oxygen extraction or gas circulation is counted as an energy source.

literature_anchor.paper: A Fuel Cell Power Supply System Equipped with Artificial Gill Membranes for Underwater Applications
demonstrated: polymer membrane harvesting dissolved oxygen from ambient water
recirculating internal gas supplying a PEM fuel cell
oxygen consumption at the fuel cell maintaining a low internal oxygen partial pressure that drives membrane transfer
prototype plus mathematical model and CFD digital twin

prototype_observation.authors_interpretation: Desktop module flow maldistribution reduced oxygen transfer relative to the idealized homogeneous-flow design.

janus_consequences: The PEMFC oxygen sink naturally supplies the collector-side low-pO2 gradient that R0/R0A required.
Direct mode removes the first-run requirement for bulk O2/N2 separation and LOX, reducing parasitic load.
Water-side convective mass transfer remains a dominant constraint; membrane material permeance alone is insufficient.
Gas recirculation, hydrogen storage/feed, water pumping, heat rejection, humidification/condensation and controls remain explicit loads.
pass_rule: P_PEMFC_electric > P_water + P_gas_recirculation + P_hydrogen_feed + P_thermal_management + P_controls + P_other_aux for a sustained operating point while O2 mass balance closes.
